jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Transportation Project Manager based in the United States.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced transportation professional to lead project delivery while helping establish and grow a regional engineering practice in Utah. You will combine technical expertise, business development, and people leadership to deliver infrastructure projects that strengthen communities and improve transportation networks. Working with multidisciplinary teams and a broad network of industry experts, you will manage project performance while building lasting client relationships. You will play an active role in shaping regional strategy, recruiting talent, and mentoring emerging professionals. With the support of established national resources and the opportunity to influence local growth, you can expand your leadership responsibilities as the practice develops. This role is ideal for an entrepreneurial, client-focused leader who wants to make a lasting impact on infrastructure and organizational growth.

Accountabilities

As a Transportation Project Manager, you will oversee project execution, develop client partnerships, and contribute to the long-term growth of the transportation practice. You will balance technical quality, commercial performance, and team development while supporting a diverse portfolio of infrastructure projects.

Lead the planning, management, and delivery of multiple transportation projects, ensuring that scope, schedules, budgets, and resources are effectively controlled.
Contribute to existing contracted project work while identifying opportunities to expand client relationships and secure new business.
Develop and maintain strong relationships with clients, public agencies, and other project stakeholders.
Support regional, local, and corporate strategic growth initiatives, helping shape the practice's direction and long-term presence in Utah.
Lead and coordinate multidisciplinary project teams, including engineers, designers, inspectors, and technologists.
Develop and oversee task work plans, ensuring that teams have clear priorities, responsibilities, and delivery expectations.
Prepare and review project communications, including meeting minutes, technical documentation, and reports.
Maintain responsibility for assigned design calculation files and ensure appropriate independent quality-control reviews are completed.
Provide guidance, mentorship, and professional development opportunities for junior staff, including those involved in design and construction-phase services.
Recruit talented professionals and help build a collaborative, high-performing team.
Apply technical and project management expertise across transportation disciplines such as roadways, structures, drainage, and traffic.
Contribute to a growing regional practice while leveraging national expertise, resources, and cross-disciplinary collaboration.

Requirements

The ideal candidate is an experienced transportation professional with strong technical credentials, proven project delivery capabilities, and a track record of developing client relationships and winning work. You should bring an entrepreneurial mindset, sound leadership skills, and the ability to contribute to both operational success and regional growth.

Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering or a closely related field.
Professional Engineer (PE) license.
At least 8 years of relevant professional experience.
Strong understanding of transportation project delivery in Utah.
Demonstrated experience managing project scope, schedules, budgets, resources, and technical deliverables.
Proven ability to develop client relationships, identify business opportunities, and win new work.
Strong business development, project management, leadership, communication, and client relationship skills.
Experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams and supporting high-quality project delivery.
Ability to recruit, mentor, and develop staff while fostering an effective team environment.
Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, particularly in technical documentation and quality assurance.
Ability to collaborate effectively with colleagues, clients, and stakeholders from varied professional backgrounds.
An entrepreneurial approach and interest in contributing to the strategic development of a growing regional practice.

Benefits

The organization offers a competitive compensation package alongside professional growth opportunities, retirement contributions, and benefits designed to support flexibility and long-term career development.

Annual salary: $124,000–$166,000 USD.
Retirement contributions: Employer contributions of up to 9% for eligible employees.
Flexible work schedules: Scheduling options designed to support professional responsibilities and personal commitments.
Paid time off: Generous paid time off to help employees rest and recharge.
Parental leave: Paid parental leave for eligible employees.
Professional development: Access to ongoing learning, mentorship, leadership training, and opportunities to build new skills.
Career advancement: Opportunities to take on greater responsibility, deepen technical expertise, and grow into broader leadership roles.
Collaborative environment: Work with experienced professionals across multiple disciplines, drawing on established resources while contributing your own expertise.
Meaningful projects: Help deliver infrastructure improvements that strengthen communities and transportation networks.
Leadership opportunities: Play an influential role in regional business development, recruitment, client relationships, and the long-term growth of the Utah practice.
Flexible location within Utah: Opportunities for candidates based along the Wasatch Front or in Southern Utah, including the Lehi, Ogden, Salt Lake City, and St. George areas.

jobs.description:
Aquent is proud to partner with a globally recognized entertainment platform that has redefined how millions interact with audio content. This trailblazing company is celebrated for its innovative spirit and dedication to cultivating a vibrant, creative ecosystem that influences global culture on an unprecedented scale. As a strategic force, you will directly empower creative teams, transforming visionary concepts into polished realities and making a tangible difference in how users engage with content worldwide, shaping the future of entertainment and impacting global culture on a massive scale.

About The Role

Are you a master organizer with a passion for bringing groundbreaking creative visions to life? This is your chance to be the essential “glue” connecting critical creative workstreams, guiding projects from initial concept through to final delivery and launch. You’ll work closely with the Creative Operations Lead, meticulously managing creative tasks, development timelines, and internal team coordination to cultivate an environment where impactful creative work thrives. Your contributions will directly influence the success of major brand initiatives and delight users globally.

Key Responsibilities

Support the Creative Operations Lead in defining creative team scope and development timelines for holistic creative projects.
Create detailed task schedules post-production commencement and assign tasks to various creative teams, including designers, copywriters, and social creatives, utilizing tools like Asana and Slack.
Act as a primary point of contact, facilitating essential communication between brand teams, creative teams, and producers.
Proactively identify and address potential project bottlenecks, risks, or scope creep, implementing effective solutions to maintain project momentum.
Conduct thorough quality assurance reviews of all creative deliverables, ensuring adherence to team requirements, quality standards, and brand guidelines prior to final delivery.
Organize and update shared drives and asset management systems with necessary project documents, files, and creative assets for the creative team.

Must-Have Qualifications

3-5 years of project management experience within a creative/advertising agency or an internal in-house studio team at a large brand.
Proficiency with project management software such as Asana, Jira, Monday.com, or Teamwork, and strong command of Google Workspace.
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate creative concepts and project updates.
A solid understanding of the creative process, encompassing design, video production, and content development.
Outstanding organizational skills, demonstrating the ability to manage multiple projects concurrently and navigate competing deadlines.

Nice-to-Have Qualifications

Experience managing digital marketing, creative development, or video production projects.
Familiarity with Adobe Creative Suite or Figma to streamline feedback loops.
Knowledge of Agile methodologies or creative sprint processes.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
Blend is a HubSpot Diamond Partner and globally recognised as the leading HubSpot website agency. With 45+ specialists across the UK and US, we partner with ambitious B2B technology companies to build connected revenue systems that fuel long-term growth.

We help organisations transform fragmented go-to-market functions into unified, AI-powered growth engines. Our work spans the full buyer journey – from creating demand through content and brand, to capturing it via websites and search, to converting it through automation and enablement.

We’re looking for an experienced Senior Project Manager to lead delivery for one of our client pods. You’ll own the delivery plan across every client in the pod, keep work moving against clearly defined milestones, and make sure the team’s time is focused where it creates the most value each week.

You’ll lead the pod in partnership with a Growth Consultant (GC). The GC owns the client relationship, the commercials, and scope decisions. You own delivery – the plan, the capacity, the milestones, the project budget and risk management. Together, you’re accountable for how your clients experience Blend and the growth they achieve with us.

How Our Pods Work

Blend’s delivery is organised into client pods: dedicated, cross-functional teams that each hold a portfolio of clients and are accountable for their outcomes, revenue, and margin. Each pod is led by a GC and a PM, with its own strategy, content, design, and development specialists, and is supported by a shared technical bench for HubSpot and AI implementation, motion, and specialist design.

You’ll report to the Project Delivery Manager (PDM), who leads Blend’s project management practice and supports your performance, development, and progression.

Key Responsibilities

Delivery planning

Own the delivery plan across every client in your pod, built around tightly defined project milestones
Once a project is approved, shape an agile delivery approach that fits its objectives, budget, and timeline, and build the milestone-based plan in Teamwork.com
Lead requirements gathering with the GC and specialists, turning the SOW into clear, documented requirements the team can deliver against
Support GC-led client kick-offs, making sure the delivery team, timeline, and dependencies are clear from day one
Keep scheduling estimates in Teamwork.com accurate, so the pod’s forward plan can be trusted when committing start dates to new clients

Capacity and the technical bench

Move capacity between clients week to week, keeping the pod focused on milestone delivery
Manage forward resource levelling meticulously, so the pod’s workload stays balanced against capacity and milestone commitments
Work with the wider Project Management Office (PMO) to agree priorities and book technical bench time for the work your clients need

Scope, risk, and escalation

Protect scope across your pod’s clients, qualifying every request against the SOW before it reaches the team
Track scope exceptions and raise anything that affects scope, cost, or a client deadline with the GC promptly, setting out the time and cost implications
Identify delivery risks and dependencies early, and bring them to the GC with recommended solutions
Make sure the information, access, and assets the team needs are in place before work starts

Quality and launch

Hold every deliverable to Blend’s quality standards, coordinating reviews, testing, and client sign-off before launch
Manage go-live and project close, including a clean handover into ongoing support or retained services
Run post-project reviews with the team, and feed the lessons into how pods deliver

Client communication

Run a consistent rhythm of delivery calls with every client in your pod – weekly, fortnightly, or monthly, depending on the size of the account
Keep clients informed on progress, upcoming milestones, and any decisions or inputs needed from them
Build confident working relationships with senior client stakeholders, and challenge constructively when delivery is at risk
Work alongside the GC, whose calls focus on the commercial relationship, so clients get one joined-up view of their work

Pod rhythm and reporting

Help run the weekly pod meeting, covering priorities, blockers, and client updates
Hold a weekly review with your GC covering scope, risks, margin to date, and the pod scorecard
Plan each six-week cycle with your pod, setting commitments the team can stand behind
Track hours planned against hours available and billable hours against budget for each client, and forecast revenue recognition against milestones
Make sure time is logged accurately against the right clients and pods, including bench time
Identify ways to improve how pods deliver, and share what works with the PDM

Pod focus

Set clear direction and expectations for the specialists in your pod, so everyone knows what they own and when it’s due
Coach and support less experienced PMs and delivery team members, sharing good practice across the PMO

How We’ll Measure Success

Every pod reports a small set of measures each week. As Senior Project Manager, you’ll own the delivery measures and the contribution margin of the completed work.

Measure / What it tracks

On-time delivery // Milestones met against milestones planned
Recognised revenue // Value of work delivered and recognised against milestones
Forward capacity // Hours available against hours planned over the next six weeks
Scope control // Scope exceptions tracked and raised to the GC
Contribution margin // Operating profit generated by the pod

How You’ll Think And Work

Beyond technical skills, we’re looking for a particular way of operating. These behaviours reflect our values and what success looks like in this role.

Delivery discipline

You bring structure to a portfolio of clients – clear plans, accurate data, and no loose ends

You plan to milestones and outcomes, not just task lists
You notice the detail others miss, without losing sight of the bigger picture

Commercial awareness

You understand that every hour has a cost, and you protect pod margin as carefully as quality
You raise scope, budget, timing, and capacity conversations early and clearly
You see how day-to-day delivery decisions shape your pod’s commercial results

Ownership and judgement

You get ahead of problems rather than reacting to them
You make sound calls on priorities within the pod, and know when a decision belongs with the GC
You resolve competing demands with other PMs constructively, with the wider business in mind
You lead by example, setting the standard for how delivery runs across your pod

Empathy

You read client dynamics and navigate tricky conversations with care
You build trust quickly through genuine curiosity and attentive listening
You challenge constructively with care for the audience

AI fluency

You’re skilled at prompting – asking better questions of both AI systems and humans to extract useful insights
You practise data sensemaking – interpreting AI outputs and contextualising them for decisions
You embrace augmentation – automating routine tasks and configuring AI projects to elevate the quality of your work
You adapt quickly – experimenting with new tools and approaches as the landscape shifts

What You Bring

Five or more years’ project management experience, including time at a senior level in a B2B, digital, business consulting, or marketing agency
A track record of leading multiple concurrent client projects to agreed milestones, on time, in scope, and on budget
Experience shaping and running agile or hybrid delivery approaches for web, CRM, or marketing technology projects
Confidence managing capacity and resource planning across a shared, cross-functional team
Strong commercial acumen, including budget management, forecasting, and change control
Credibility with senior client stakeholders, and the confidence to influence and challenge
Excellent written and verbal communication
Advanced use of project management tools (Teamwork.com or similar)
Proven experience applying AI and automation to enhance workflows

Desirable

Experience working in a pod, squad, or similar cross-functional team model
Experience mentoring or line-managing project managers
Experience delivering HubSpot website and implementation projects
Experience working with US clients across time zones
HubSpot certifications
A recognised project management qualification (for example, PMP, ISO, APM, PRINCE2, or Scrum)

Why Blend

Work with leading B2B brands across high-tech manufacturing, fintech, and cyber
Exposure to advanced HubSpot implementations, AEO strategies, and RevOps
Collaborative environment with 45+ professionals across the UK and US
Hybrid working from our Reading office: 3 days in-office for collaboration, 2 days remote for focused work
25 days’ annual leave plus bank holidays, increasing by one day for each year of service (up to 28 days total)
Professional development support, including HubSpot certifications and training
Shape processes and contribute to growth

We look forward to hearing from you.

new_jobs.description:
Silicon Quantum Computing (SQC) is at the forefront of global efforts to build the world’s first commercial-scale quantum computer, while delivering quantum-enhanced AI and simulation products to customers today.

Backed by over 25 years of technological excellence, SQC is a full-stack quantum computing company that leverages its proprietary manufacturing process to engineer atomic qubits in silicon with 0.13 nanometer precision. It is the most precise semiconductor manufacturing in the world, enabling systems with world-leading algorithmic fidelity, and a decisive advantage in the global quantum computing race.

Our products are commercially deployed and generating revenue. Watermelon, our quantum-enhanced AI system, is delivering superior results on real-world problems across energy, telecom and finance. Quantum Twins, our simulation platform, provides unparalleled ability to model quantum systems, accelerating molecule and materials discovery.

This is SQC: building the future of computing while delivering quantum impact today.

About The Role

SQC builds gate-based quantum computers in silicon. Our largest programs are multi-year commitments to US government sponsors, delivered against fixed benchmarks, milestones and independent evaluation. We are hiring a Technical Project Manager (Embedded) into Projects to own the hardware and software delivery schedule for the USQC program.

You will own the detailed schedule end to end for the embedded hardware and software work.You will hold a critical path that runs through fabrication, cryogenic test, firmware and software release, and external partner deliverables. Predictability is the core of the job. You will flag early when a tapeout or release is at risk, and when a test result or blocker lands, you will replan quickly and make the consequences clear to the people who need to act on them.

You will work directly with the hardware and software engineering leads on technical readiness, including test plans, release criteria and the hand-off between design, fabrication and integration. You will also manage the embedded partners and subcontractors whose deliverables feed the tapeout and software schedules.

You will report to the Senior Technical Program Manager. Escalate commercial priorities, scope changes and government requirements to them rather than absorbing them into the embedded plan.

Based at our Sydney facility, you will work across the hardware and software teams, moving between technical detail with engineers, clear synthesis for management, and concise updates for the executive and the CEO. This is a role for someone with a genuine project management mindset: structured, disciplined about following defined processes, personally committed to milestones, and comfortable challenging engineering estimates and pushing back when delivery slips.

Role Responsibilities

Own the schedule for cryogenic and conventional ASIC tapeouts, from design freeze through fabrication, characterisation, and foundry coordination.
Own the delivery schedule for compiler, decoder and real-time control plane software releases, including the release train and the R&D deliverables that depend on them.
Build and maintain a credible critical path across hardware, firmware and software, through fabrication, measurement and subcontractor deliverables.
Flag tapeout, foundry, and release risks early, then drive replanning and communicate schedule, cost, and technical impacts.
Plan and track FPGA hardware development, from requirements through deployment.
Plan and track cryogenic interface and control system development, including coordination with external technology partners.
Define test readiness and release criteria with the hardware and software leads and track them to closure.
Run structured risk assessment for each embedded workstream, with a mitigation plan for every dependency.
Hold engineering teams to their commitments, challenge estimates, and escalate slippage to the Senior Technical Program Manager.
Apply SDLC and quality processes consistently across the embedded teams.
Communicate with engineers in technical detail, and with management in concise summaries.

Your Experience

Experience with embedded systems, including FPGA development.
Experience with software release management or SDLC, ideally on compiler, firmware or FPGA workstreams.
A track record of delivering hardware or embedded programs against fixed external milestones, where the deadline does not move.
Experience owning detailed schedules across hardware and software workstreams, including external partners and subcontractors.
Experience managing external partners or suppliers delivering into a hardware program.
A background in semiconductor, test engineering, embedded systems or hardware program management, where hardware dependencies carry real schedule risk.
A structured approach to risk, identifying dependencies early and maintaining credible mitigation plans.
Experience with Agile delivery (Scrum or Kanban) across hardware and software teams.
Willing to hold the line, challenging estimates and pushing back when delivery slips.
Strong communication across engineers and management in a matrix environment.
Comfortable operating to defined processes and formal quality requirements.
A fast learner, comfortable picking up quantum and cryogenic vocabulary on the job. Experience on government-funded programs is desirable.

Equal opportunity

SQC is an equal opportunity employer. We value diverse perspectives and experiences, and encourage applications from candidates who may not meet every listed requirement. If you’re excited about the role and believe you can contribute, we encourage you to apply.

Export controls

This position may require access to export-controlled information or technology. Employment may be subject to applicable export control laws and may require eligibility assessment based on factors such as nationality, citizenship, or residency, and, where necessary, obtaining relevant export licenses or approvals.

About SQC

SQC was founded by renowned physicist and materials scientist Michelle Simmons, who pioneered the field of atomic electronics, including the development of the world’s first single-atom transistor and the first integrated circuit built with atomic precision. Our Chair, Simon Segars, former CEO of Arm, is a leader in the semiconductor industry and was instrumental in developing the processors that powered the mobile computing revolution.

As a full-stack company with in-house QPU manufacturing, SQC can design, produce and test new quantum chips in under a week, enabling rapid iteration and a decisive advantage in the race to build the world’s first commercial-scale quantum computer.

SQC is a high-accountability environment built on a simple principle: Every Atom Counts. If you’re looking to play a meaningful role in building the next frontier of computing, we’d love to hear from you.

Job Description

BAE Systems is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Program Manager to support our Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) Futures Division, specifically within the Advanced Capabilities and Integration Branch. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to the future of strategic deterrence by supporting experimental flight testing and payload integration for next-generation technologies and capabilities within the ICBM Systems Directorate.

This Program Manager will be an integral part of a highly skilled team providing programmatic support for the LGM-35A Sentinel and future ICBM development efforts. You will play a critical role in ensuring the successful integration of experimental payloads and the smooth execution of flight test programs.

The candidate will operate in an organizational culture that develops and challenges employees to achieve high performance in a fast-paced, high-morale workplace using streamlined management policies and procedures. It is a challenging and rewarding position with growth opportunity, backed by, and integrated with the broad technology-related capabilities of BAE Systems, Inc. as one of the top 10 DoD contractors. You will provide contributions that will shape the development and deployment of the US Air Force’s next generation ICBM and support similar efforts to integrate aerospace systems engineering, integration, and test capabilities with US Space Force and others within BAE Systems’ broad DoD customer base.

Why BAE Systems? BAE Systems is the third largest defense contractor in the world with an exceptional, mission-focused culture. The BAE Systems employees and sub-contractors located at Hill Air Force Base, Utah are predominantly aligned to the ICBM Systems Directorate, Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center. We support the directorate in sustaining the existing LGM-30 Minuteman III (MM III) weapon system and acquiring its replacement, the Sentinel ICBM. We are a uniquely valued mission partner delivering daily technical excellence and innovative solutions to the Government. BAE Systems has earned accolades as a “Top Workplace” in Utah based on employee feedback for seven consecutive years, earning special distinction for providing a healthy work-life balance for our valued employees. We work very hard to ensure this is a great place to work!

Why Utah? You’ve got to see it to believe it! Utah is an amazing state with diverse geography, an eclectic culture, and an exceptional quality of life. We are located north of Salt Lake City at the foot of the beautiful Wasatch Mountains. The area offers an incredible range of outdoors pursuits across the seasons including hiking, climbing, hunting, fishing, camping, boating and world-class skiing at resorts that hosted the 2002 Winter Olympics, and will do so again in 2032. The state is home to five amazing National Parks and an easy drive from two more; Grand Teton and, famously, the first National Park in the world, Yellowstone. The Salt Lake City area offers a vast array of cultural activities and businesses including multiple professional sports teams. It is a western states hub for exceptional, cutting-edge medical care with people traveling from across the region for a range of nationally renowned specialty care centers and doctors. The Salt Lake International Airport is expanding and offers easy, direct access to just about anywhere you want to fly.

This is a rare opportunity to join a high-performing team within a large defense company with an extraordinary, positive culture and mission focus. In this position, you will provide direct support to a national security-critical weapon system through engineering development, deployment, and sustainment activities. You will help shape the quality and performance of engineering and technical products from several hundred personnel supporting the Government, and you will help educate and equip the Government to acquire, operate, and maintain an entire weapon system-of-systems. You will become a trusted mission partner to innovative, digital engineering-driven Air and Space Force organizations that are responsible for designing, building, testing, deploying, and sustaining the world’s safest, most secure, and effective land-based nuclear deterrent and other national security capabilities. Do not miss this once-in-a-lifetime opportunity!

Pursuant to Government contract, this position requires US Citizenship status.

Excellent cognitive, communication (both written and spoken), and interpersonal skills, with the ability to clearly articulate complex technical concepts.

About This Role

负责新产品开发项目全生命周期管理，带领跨职能团队高效交付项目，包括但不限于项目沟通、工程开发管理、制造可行性评估、生产过程与质量控制，以及其他项目运营中的关键问题。

In this role, you will be responsible for the end-to-end lifecycle management of new product development projects, leading cross-functional teams to deliver projects efficiently. This includes, but is not limited to, project communication, engineering development management, manufacturing feasibility assessment, production process and quality control, and other critical operational issues within projects.

Key Responsibilities

项目全生命周期管理：同时负责2个或以上大项目或复杂项目，主导新产品从概念，设计开发，试产，验证到量产及爬坡的全过程，确保项目按计划完成。
跨职能团队领导：领导全球跨职能团队，管理日常沟通，主持项目例会，确保团队清晰理解项目要求、质量标准和交付目标。
核心沟通与汇报：定期向高管及跨部门干系人汇报项目进展。组织项目各阶段报告会议，向管理层及干系人清晰、透明地汇报项目进展、里程碑及核心指标。
工程开发管理：领导跨职能工程团队进行产品设计、开发及验证，确保设计符合产品需求，技术规格及安规要求。
制造可行性评估：主导新产品设计的制造可行性和测试可行性评估，推动设计优化以实现最佳可制造性。
生产过程与质量控制：在试产和量产阶段，监督生产流程，协同运营团队解决生产制程问题、良率提升和产品质量问题。
运营与供应链协同：监控整个新产品导入过程中的物料准备状况，识别并解决供应链瓶颈，确保生产连续性。
End-to-End Project Lifecycle Management:

Oversee two or more large-scale or complex projects concurrently, leading the entire process from concept, design, development, trial runs, validation, mass production and ramp-up. Ensure projects are completed on schedule.

Cross-Functional Team Leadership:

Lead global cross-functional teams, manage day-to-day communication, host regular project meetings, and ensure the team has a clear understanding of project requirements, quality standards, and delivery goals.

Core Communication and Reporting:

Regularly report project progress to executives and cross-departmental stakeholders. Organize phase-gate review meetings and provide clear, transparent reports to management and stakeholders on project progress, milestones, and key metrics.

Engineering Development Management:

Lead cross-functional engineering teams in product design, development and validation to ensure compliance with product requirements, technical specifications and safety regulations.

Manufacturing Feasibility Assessment:

Drive manufacturing and test feasibility evaluations for new product designs. Promote design optimization to achieve best-in-class manufacturability.

Production Process and Quality Control:

During trial runs and mass production phases, monitor manufacturing processes and collaborate with operations teams to resolve process issues, improve yield and address product quality concerns.

Operations and Supply Chain Coordination:

Monitor material readiness throughout the New Product Introduction (NPI) process. Identify and resolve supply chain bottlenecks to ensure production continuity.

全日制大学本科或以上，电子工程类相关专业毕业。

Help

Performs information technology (IT) project business management duties; focusing and synchronizing DISA and customer efforts to achieve goals and increase operational effectiveness through a unified enterprise-wide project management approach.
Meets with key customer and coordinating officials to assess customer satisfaction, explains organization policies and procedures, and resolves problems that arise.
Participates in special projects and initiatives and performs special assignments.
Develops Mission Partner portfolios and strategic plans to assist the mission partner in the oversight and financial management of existing capabilities, as well as the planning and delivery of future requirements.

Requirements

Help

Qualifications

In order to qualify for this position, you must meet the requirements described below.

In addition to meeting the basic requirement, applicants must possess qualifying experience.
To qualify based on your experience, your resume must describe at least one year of experience that demonstrates the competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Experience refers to any paid or unpaid experience, including volunteer work and Military service, that would be considered equivalent to work normally performed at the next lower grade level in the federal service.

experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been responsible for reviewing the work of others to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards.

briefing senior-level management and IT staff on the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the communication of complex technical information to a non-technical audience.

identifying alternatives to address unique, highly complex, or sensitive information technology-related issues. I have anticipated information technology-related problems and have identified and evaluated potential sources of information to generate alternative solutions.

Qualifying Experience

To qualify at the GG-15 grade level, your resume must describe at least one year of experience that demonstrates the competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Experience refers to any paid or unpaid experience, including volunteer work and Military service, that would be considered equivalent to work normally performed at the next lower grade level in the federal service.

For this position, qualifying experience is defined as: Experience managing mission partner outreach and relationships; OR managing enterprise-wide governance; OR synchronizing mission partner efforts to increase operational effectiveness.

Candidates must describe how they meet the qualifying experience and/or selective placement factor(s) within the body of their resume. All qualifications must be met within 30 days after the closing date of this announcement.

Education

There is no substitution of education for the
qualifying experienceat the GG-15 grade level.

Are you an experienced Project Manager who thrives on bringing structure, pace and control to complex technical projects?
We're looking for a confident, commercially aware Project Manager to join Netteam tX, taking ownership of the successful delivery of customer IT projects from initial handover through to completion. This is a hands-on, customer-facing role where you'll manage larger and more complex projects yourself, while also helping us drive consistency, visibility and strong project management across our wider portfolio.
You'll take end-to-end ownership of technical customer projects, ensuring they are properly scoped, planned, resourced and commercially controlled before and throughout delivery.
Day to day, you'll:

Manage complex technical projects from sales handover and mobilisation through to delivery, customer acceptance, handover and closure.
Build and maintain clear project plans, actions, risks, dependencies, milestones and target dates.
Coordinate technical engineers, internal teams, customers and third-party suppliers.
Own customer communication throughout the project lifecycle, ensuring expectations are clear and issues are addressed early.
Manage project budgets, sold versus actual hours, margin, forecasting, change control and billing readiness.
Identify projects that are at risk of delay, overspend or scope creep and put clear recovery plans in place.
Ensure additional or out-of-scope work is properly assessed, documented, priced and approved.
Work closely with Sales and Pre-Sales to ensure projects entering delivery have a clear scope, appropriate technical design and validated customer prerequisites.
Support effective resource and capacity planning across Professional Services.
Maintain accurate and up-to-date project information within our PSA platform.
Provide clear project and portfolio reporting, highlighting risks, resource constraints, financial exposure and decisions required.
Help continually improve our project processes, governance, reporting and customer handovers.

Our projects encompass a broad variety of technologies and customer requirements, including Microsoft 365 and Azure, cloud and server migrations, networking, firewalls, switching and Wi-Fi, cybersecurity, backup and disaster recovery, telephony, customer onboarding, office moves, hardware refreshes and new-site deployments. We also deliver technology projects within the hospitality sector, including hotel-system upgrades, migrations and integrations.
About you:

You'll already have strong project management experience, ideally gained within an IT Managed Service Provider (MSP) or similarly fast-paced technology environment.
You'll be comfortable managing multiple projects and competing priorities at the same time, but equally willing to get into the detail when a particular project needs your attention.
We'd particularly like to hear from you if you have:
Proven experience managing customer-facing IT or technology projects.
Experience working within an MSP or fast-moving IT services environment.
Strong customer and stakeholder management skills.
Confidence managing escalations and challenging conversations.
Commercial awareness and experience managing project budgets, hours, margin and scope changes.
A disciplined approach to project planning, risk management, dependencies and governance.
The ability to coordinate technical resources without needing to be the technical expert yourself.
The confidence to challenge incomplete information or unclear scope before delivery begins.
Strong organisation skills and the ability to keep control across multiple concurrent projects.

Experience using Autotask PSA or a similar MSP PSA platform would be particularly valuable. Project management qualifications such as PRINCE2, APM, AgilePM or PMP would be advantageous, although practical experience delivering successfully within an MSP environment is more important to us.
You don't need to be an engineer. What matters is that you understand technology well enough to ask the right questions, recognise risks and bring together the right technical people to deliver the solution.
You'll be someone who remains calm when projects become difficult, communicates clearly with customers, spots problems before they become major issues and is comfortable taking ownership rather than simply reporting that something has gone wrong. You'll combine attention to detail with commercial awareness and be confident balancing customer commitments, resource availability, deadlines and project profitability. US. citizenship and willingness to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance.

Active U.S. Government security clearance, with SSBI/SCI eligibility.

Master’s degree in relevant engineering, science, or business discipline.
Experience with U.S. Government contracting and execution of development programs.

Manages the operational, personnel, and financial aspects of the Trauma Program, as appropriate. Assist with the budgetary process for the Trauma Program.
Coordinate management across the continuum of trauma care, including the planning and implementation of clinical protocols and practice management guidelines, monitoring of in-hospital patients, and serving as a resource for clinical practice.

Perform administrative functions, include initiating, developing, planning, and evaluating activities of the Trauma Center’s mission of providing optimal trauma care, as defined by the American College of Surgeons Resources for Optimal Care of the Injured Patient.
Maintain all forms of HIPPA and trauma patient confidentiality.
Collaborate with the Trauma Medical Director in the formulation of standards or performance, evaluation, and supervision of the Trauma Center’s clinical support staff.
Demonstrate active involvement in research projects and the analysis and distribution of findings. Facilitate protocol design for accurate data collection, feedback, and analysis as applicable for the facility.

Stabilize the complex network of the many disciplines that work in concert to provide high-quality care. Serve as an internal resource for staff in all departments and act as an extended liaison for EMS agencies.
Participate in the implementation and evaluation of programs supporting pre-hospital care, transportation, acute hospitalization, and rehabilitation care issues.
Support the Trauma Program through astute accuracy of all reports and timely submission of data to entities which provide funding for trauma care.
Conduct Trauma Department meetings in partnership with the Trauma Medical Director.

Assume responsibility for the development of processes for monitoring and improving the financial performance and resource utilization of the Trauma Center.

Provide professional staff development and direct community trauma education and prevention programs.
Maintain open lines of communication with regional hospital administrators, physicians, nurses and pre-hospital care providers. Provide feedback to referring physicians, nurses, and EMS agencies.
Demonstrate commitment to maintaining market share through patient and consumer education and by improving patient and consumer satisfaction.

The Regional Medical Operations Coordination Center (RMOCC) Data Analyst (East/West Liaison) supports the collection, validation, analysis, and communication of regional healthcare and EMS data. The East regional liaison data analyst will coordinate with the University of Kentucky (UK) team, while the West regional liaison data analyst will coordinate with the University of Louisville (UofL) in line with a consistent RMOCC operating model. The data analyst will translate operational data into timely, decision-relevant information for RMOCC leadership and regional partners, working closely with the counterpart analyst to align data practices across regions, identify capacity and patient-flow trends, support dashboards and recurring reports, and improve data quality and usability. The analyst will also support the monitoring, analysis, and reporting of Pulsara utilization and transfer coordination data, helping identify opportunities to improve interfacility communication, patent movement, and regional resource coordination. During RMOCC activations or surge events, the analyst may provide data and situational awareness support within the established command and escalation structure.

Regional Data Liaison and Coordination
Serve as the primary RMOCC data liaison for the assigned East/UK or West/UofL region, maintaining regular communication with participating EMS agencies, hospitals, and other designated partners.
Coordinate with the counterpart East/West analyst to apply consistent data definitions, submission schedules, validation rules, and reporting formats across both regions.
Gather regional data needs and operational questions, translate them into clear analytical requirements, and elevate cross-regional issues to RMOCC leadership.

Pulsara is a secure clinical communication and care coordination platform being implemented across Kentucky to support real-time communication, patient routing, and interfacility coordination among EMS agencies, hospitals, and healthcare partners. Within the RMOCC model, Pulsara will serve as a key enabling technology for regional situational awareness, care coordination, and patient transfer management.

new_jobs.title: Senior Business Analyst Reshopping - Barcelona or London
new_jobs.description:
About FCM

FCM is more than a global travel management company with 24/7 support in 100+ countries. We’re a movement, 6,500+ changemakers, travel experts, and performance drivers redefining corporate travel. We don’t just keep the world’s biggest companies moving, we make it smoother, smarter, and bolder. Certified as a great place to work and fuelled by an alternative mindset, we embrace change, challenge convention, and do things differently. This is FCM, where different happens.

About The Opportunity

We're looking for a Senior Business Analyst to define and answer the right questions that will help us shape and drive our Reshopping program. Reshopping continuously monitors booked hotel reservations and air itineraries and secures better rates and fares on behalf of some of the world's largest corporate travel programs. Scaling it globally means committing to a series of consequential decisions regarding the target market, our customers’ needs, and which parts of the capability we build ourselves versus source from a partner.

Your job is to go and get the understanding and evidence — from our markets, our customers, and the vendor landscape — and to set out what you find clearly. Your findings sit at the centre of every major call we make on Reshopping: which markets, which partners, and what we build ourselves. You will work directly with the Program Leader and Product Managers, and you will be in the room when those decisions are made.

You will report to the Program Leader, Reshopping, and work across both hotel and air.

Location

This role can be based in one of our major offices in Barcelona or London. Fully remote may be considered for the right applicant.

Key Responsibilities

Investigate and document the specifics of our reshopping offering in each of our markets — the operational, regulatory, invoicing, and supplier differences that determine what is possible where.
Research customer and prospect needs across large-market and SME programs, so that what we build reflects demand rather than assumption.
Map the vendor and partner landscape for post-booking cost optimization: what each provider does, where they are strong, and what integrating with them would require.
Map the reshopping value chain — opportunity monitoring, decisioning, servicing, measurement, and invoicing — and set out which parts we rent, buy, partner, or build, balancing flexibility, speed, and commercial and financial benefit, so that the Program Leader and Product Managers have a clear basis to decide on.
Build and maintain the financial KPIs and metrics behind the offering, and identify where the greatest opportunities sit across hotel and air.
Document the commercial and operational lifecycle around the reshopping offering, including manual steps and local variation.
Determine and document system, business, and development dependencies, ensuring a seamless delivery.
Proactively keep abreast of new technologies emerging within the industry, both regionally and globally, and make recommendations on alternate products and options.
Contribute to a safe, inclusive, accessible, and fun work environment where all Flighties feel welcomed, respected, and supported to thrive.

Experience & Qualifications

5+ years in business analysis, including work where the answer was not known at the outset.
A track record of primary discovery — structured conversations with customers, internal teams, and vendors — and of turning it into something decision-ready.
Proven at evaluating vendors and partners on capability, fit, and integration cost rather than on feature lists.
Grounded in corporate travel or travel technology, including supplier commercial models, post-booking servicing, and managed travel program economics.
Fluent in hotel and air content — negotiated and public rates and fares, rate and fare rules, and cancellation and change conditions.
Strong at building a quantified case from large transactional datasets.
Skilled at defining measurement methodologies that stand up to customer and finance scrutiny.
Able to separate what the evidence supports from what you believe, and to present both clearly.
Comfortable working across many markets and time zones.
Confident writing requirements precise enough for engineers to build from.
Degree in Technology, Business, or a related field preferred.

Your Benefits (Please Note, This Differs By Region)

Enjoy 25 Days Off per year plus 5 Compensation days!
Learn a new language with our free language learning platform.
Employee Retention Share Scheme.
Various social events to promote networking, the celebration of wins, and sometimes just for fun!
Enjoy our discounts with GymApp.
Complimentary coffee, drinks, snacks and fruits at our Barcelona office location.
A strong focus on professional development to support you in the evolution of your career.

new_jobs.title: Compliance Operations Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Help shape fair and meaningful customer outcomes at Zip, taking ownership of complex external disputes and driving improvements that make a real difference.
Bring your experience in financial services, compliance or dispute resolution, with knowledge of AFCA or similar external dispute resolution frameworks.
Permanent, Sydney based individual contributor role, collaborating with teams across Risk and Compliance, Customer Service, Credit, Fraud and Product.

Write your story with a career at Zip

Join Zip's Risk and Compliance team, helping our businesses deliver fair customer outcomes while meeting our regulatory and compliance obligations. We're a collaborative team that brings together risk expertise, sound judgement and a Customer First mindset to help the business navigate complex challenges and continuously improve how we work.

As our Compliance Operations Analyst, you'll play an important role in managing external disputes and privacy requests, ensuring customers receive fair, timely and well considered outcomes.

Working with external dispute resolution bodies including the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA) and you'll manage complex matters, build effective stakeholder relationships and help strengthen Zip's approach to dispute resolution.

Beyond resolving individual cases, you'll use complaint insights to identify emerging risks, improve processes and contribute to a proactive, customer focused compliance environment.

What You’ll Own

Manage a portfolio of external dispute resolution complaints from investigation through to resolution, delivering fair, timely outcomes in line with regulatory requirements and relevant dispute resolution frameworks.
Prepare clear, balanced and well structured submissions to external dispute resolution bodies, bringing together evidence, customer circumstances and regulatory considerations.
Manage requests received through Zip's Australian and New Zealand privacy inboxes, ensuring responses are accurate, timely and aligned with applicable privacy obligations.
Coordinate the EDR workflow, including case allocation, escalation of complex matters and monitoring progress to support timely resolution.
Build effective working relationships with external dispute resolution bodies and internal stakeholders, helping resolve sensitive and complex customer matters.
Partner with Customer Service, Credit, Fraud and Product teams to investigate complaints, identify underlying issues and improve customer experiences.
Analyse complaint data to identify trends, systemic issues, emerging risks and control gaps, translating insights into practical recommendations.
Prepare meaningful reporting for risk and compliance governance forums, highlighting key themes, customer impacts and opportunities for improvement.
Contribute to the ongoing development of Zip's EDR framework, strengthening processes, controls and ways of working across products.
Support quality assurance and peer reviews to maintain consistent, high quality dispute handling and regulatory compliance.
Share your knowledge with colleagues and business stakeholders, supporting training and capability development in dispute resolution and complaints management.
Identify opportunities to improve efficiency and customer outcomes through smarter processes, automation and the thoughtful use of AI and new tools.

What You’ll Bring To The Team

Zipsters work on a broad range of initiatives, and our skills and experiences all look a little different. What really matters to us is that you’re a great fit with our four Values, and have a desire to learn and grow.

So whether you meet some or all of the desirable attributes below, we’d still love to hear from you:

Around 6+ years of experience in compliance, legal, dispute resolution or financial services, with exposure to external dispute resolution processes and regulatory requirements.
Knowledge of AFCA or similar external dispute resolution frameworks, with experience engaging external bodies and managing customer complaints.
Strong written communication skills, with the ability to prepare clear, balanced submissions and explain complex matters in a way that is easy to understand.
Sound judgement and a customer focused approach to managing sensitive disputes, balancing regulatory obligations, fairness and commercial considerations.
Strong analytical and problem solving capabilities, with the ability to identify complaint trends, investigate root causes and recommend practical improvements.
Experience navigating customer service and administrative systems to gather information, review evidence and support thorough investigations.
Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities, fluctuating caseloads and regulatory deadlines.
A collaborative approach to working with stakeholders across different business functions, building trust and contributing to shared outcomes.
A proactive and curious mindset, with an interest in improving dispute resolution processes, controls and customer experiences.
A mindset that embraces AI and new tools to adapt, learn and grow.
An aptitude for identifying and managing risks. Whether you are a People Manager or an Individual Contributor, we are all leaders at Zip, therefore effective risk management is important to how we run our business and part of all our roles.
Our values in your DNA. Customer First, Own It, Stronger Together and Change the Game.

What You’ll Get In Return

As we write this next exciting chapter in our story, we will continue to move at pace and embrace change. For you, this might mean opportunities to learn new skills with hands-on experience, broader responsibilities, or the buzz of seeing your work impact customers faster.

Zip is a place where you’ll get out exactly what you put in. When you join the team, we'll do our best to make sure you can be yourself and surround yourself with smart, friendly colleagues and leaders who have your back, so that you can make the big things happen.

Zipsters tell us these are just some of the best things about working here. You’ll also receive:

25 days paid leave annually, including birthday leave and quarterly wellbeing days
16 weeks paid parental leave for primary carers, and 4 weeks for supporting carers
Family support policies including miscarriage bereavement leave and domestic violence leave
Mental health and wellness initiatives, including $299 annual wellbeing allowance, free access for you and family members to our Wellbeing platform Sonder, discounted private health insurance, and great rates on fitness sessions through ClassPass
2 days paid volunteering leave, 2 days study leave and 2 days religious or cultural leave per year
Fee-free Zip products, and discounts with Zip merchant partners (AU)
Team social events, epic offices, free breakfast daily, and weekly free lunches (Sydney and Melbourne)
Access the Flare Benefits Hub & Novated Leasing: Save on groceries, fuel, tech, fashion, dining and more, with exclusive health perks, wellbeing guidance and potential tax savings on car ownership.

Be a part of a team that reflects the diversity of our customers

We pride ourselves on being a workplace that provides equal opportunities to people of all ages, cultural backgrounds, sexual orientations, gender identities, abilities, veteran status, and everything else that makes you unique.

Equally, we’re committed to ensuring our recruitment processes are accessible and inclusive. Please let us know if there are any adjustments that need to be made to ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

And finally…get to know us

Zip Co Limited (ASX: ZIP) is a digital financial services company, offering innovative, people-centred products.

In Australia and New Zealand, Zip offers access to point of sale credit and digital payment services, connecting customers with merchant partners and helping people take control of how they pay.

We're proud to be a values led business and our values, Customer First, Own It, Stronger Together and Change the Game, guide us in everything we do.

Ramsay provides high quality healthcare to millions of people each year through a network of hospitals, clinics and services in Australia, Europe and the United Kingdom.

Job Description

We are hiring for a Junior Data Analyst to join our Finance & Business Intelligence team at Joondalup Health Campus. This is the perfect launchpad to develop your analytical skills, rapidly scale your technical capabilities, and gain hands-on experience driving real business decisions.

Working alongside experienced analysts and stakeholders across the business, you will help transform raw data into meaningful insights, contribute to reporting and visualisation, and support the ongoing improvement of our data and reporting processes.

We are looking for someone with a strong analytical mindset, an eagerness to learn, and an interest in understanding how data can be used to solve business problems. You will be supported to build your skills and take on increasing responsibility as you develop in the role.

As a Junior Data Analyst your role will include, but is not limited to:

Data preparation and analysis: Extracting, cleaning, transforming, and validating data to prepare it for analysis and reporting.
Reporting and visualisation: Assisting with the development and maintenance of reports and dashboards to communicate business performance, trends, and insights.
Business insights: Analysing financial and operational data to identify patterns, investigate variances, and help answer business questions.
Data management and governance: Maintaining documentation, data definitions, and processes to support data quality, consistency, and governance requirements.
Business collaboration: Working with stakeholders to understand their reporting needs, clarify business requirements, and communicate findings in a clear and accessible way.
Continuous improvement: Contributing ideas to improve reporting, analytical processes, and the use of data across the business.
Learning and development: Building your technical and analytical skills through hands-on experience, collaboration with experienced team members, and ongoing professional development.

What We Are Looking For

We value potential, curiosity, and a strong analytical mindset. While previous industry experience is not essential, you should be keen to learn, comfortable working with numbers, and motivated to develop your skills as a data analyst.

To Succeed In This Role, You Will Bring

Relevant qualifications: A degree in Data Analytics, Data Science, Statistics, or Computer Science. You will have a strong foundation in quantitative analysis and an interest in applying data to business problems.
Foundational technical skills: An understanding of data analysis and manipulation, with exposure to tools such as Microsoft Excel and SQL through studies, projects, internships, or other practical experience.
Reporting and visualisation: An interest in presenting data visually. Exposure to Power BI or similar reporting tools is advantageous but not essential.
Analytical thinking: The ability to investigate problems, recognise patterns and trends, interpret results, and ask thoughtful questions about what the data is telling you.
Attention to detail: A methodical approach to working with data, with an appreciation for accuracy, data quality, and reliable reporting.
Communication and collaboration: The ability to explain findings clearly, work effectively with others, and adapt your communication to different audiences.
Initiative and a willingness to learn: A proactive attitude, an openness to feedback, and a desire to develop new technical skills and continuously improve.

What’s In It For You

At Ramsay, we care for our people by offering benefits that truly support your career, wellbeing and lifestyle, including:

Grow your career with recognition programs, employee referral bonuses, scholarships, free access to LinkedIn Learning and the Ramsay Leadership Academy
Save more every day with Ramsay Rewards, giving you exclusive deals at 100+ retailers, restaurants, travel providers and more
Enjoy peace of mind with lower hospital cover costs and higher extras limits on services like General and Major Dental, plus pharmacy and allied health discounts
Find balance through flexible rostering options, flexible leave and access to free, confidential counselling and wellbeing support 24/7
Increase your take-home pay through novated leasing, plus discounts on leisure travel, gyms and lifestyle services.

Why Join Ramsay

At Ramsay Health Care, “people caring for people” is at the heart of everything we do. We are:

Australia’s largest private hospital operator, with over 74 sites and 35,000 staff
A values-led workplace where you’ll be supported personally and professionally
A place with flexible, permanent and career-growth opportunities nationwide.

Additional Information

Must provide or complete a National Police Check conducted within the previous 12 months.
According to the role, Ramsay may require a Working-With-Children Check and proof of immunisation against infectious diseases.

Apply

To be considered for this role, you must submit all three of the following:

CV

Please submit your CV including any relevant academic results and qualifications.

Data Project Summary (one-page PDF)

Summary

A one-page PDF summarising a data-related project completed as part of your studies, an internship, employment or an independent project. Structure your summary into three paragraphs covering:

The problem: What data-related problem or question were you trying to address?
The approach: What methodology, analytical techniques and tools did you use?
The outcome: What insights did you uncover, and how could these inform a decision, solve a problem or deliver value?

You may use an individual or group project. For group projects, clearly describe your own contribution. We are interested in your analytical thinking, approach to problem-solving and ability to communicate findings, rather than the complexity of the project or the number of tools used.

Covering Letter

Please include a covering letter addressing both of the following questions:

How do your current technical and analytical skills relate to the specific responsibilities of this role? Provide examples where possible.
What specifically interests you about joining our hospital, and how do you see this role contributing to the organisation?

Please ensure all documents are included, as incomplete applications may not be considered.

Ready to feel cared for while you care for others? Apply today. All applications are to be lodged online.

Applications close: 24/11/2026

Ramsay Health Care is committed to Child Safety. Details of our commitment are set out in our Code of Conduct, available at www.ramsayhealth.com.au.

Business Analyst / Associate Product Manager
new_jobs.description:
Requirements

3+ years as a BA, Product Analyst or Product Owner in fintech, billing, e-commerce or another domain where money is counted and reconciled.
Ownership Mindset: You bring a recommended option with reasoning, flag what you assumed and what you traded away, and know which decisions are yours and which belong to someone else.
Requirements Writing: Specs with clear scope, acceptance criteria and explicit non-goals - not a list of wishes. User stories, use cases, process modelling.
API Literacy: Comfortable with OpenAPI specs, JSON payloads, REST semantics, webhooks and asynchronous callbacks. You don't write code, but you can reason about idempotency and state transitions.
Data Skills: SQL at a level that lets you check how a rule behaves on real data before writing it into a spec, and read your own metrics after release.
Async System Logic: Understanding that transaction states, retries and reconciliation must be specified rather than assumed.
Rapid Prototyping: Able to put together a clickable or visual prototype quickly - including with AI tools - to agree a flow with the business and hand a designer something concrete rather than a description.
Documentation Tooling: Confluence and Jira - specs, epic decomposition, decision log.
Language: English B1+ (provider documentation, specs and part of the backlog are in English).

Responsibilities

Product work:

Own Features End to End: Take a business need - merchants can't withdraw their own balance, fees are opaque, a region needs a new provider - and drive it to release. Define the outcome, the scope, and what's explicitly out of scope for the first phase.
Scope to a Minimal Complete Scenario: Identify the smallest business flow that works end to end and delivers value - including its provider dependencies, finance dependencies, and the operational procedures that have to exist for it to run in production.
Close Questions, Escalate Risks: Propose a reasoned option rather than a list of alternatives. Document assumptions and trade-offs, resolve questions within agreed authority, and escalate material risks early rather than late.
Prioritise: Argue why this feature before that one, using actual data - transaction volumes, failure rates, support load, provider costs.
Work With Stakeholders: Translate between finance, business development and engineering. Each describes the same problem in a different language.

Analysis Work

Model Money Flows: Specify holds, settlements, refunds, fees and ledger entries. Define what happens on cancel, reject, timeout and provider failure - which balance moves, when, and by how much.
Specify Reconciliation: Define how discrepancies are detected, investigated and corrected - what the system flags, what the operator sees, which adjustments are allowed and who may make them.
Write Specs That Hold Together: Complete rules, no internal contradictions, explicit non-goals. A spec is done when an engineer can build from it without guessing and a tester can verify against it without asking.
Decompose Epics Into a Critical Path: Split a feature into backend, frontend and admin work, mark blocking dependencies, flag external blockers before the team starts.
Define Access and Permissions: Specify role-based access, tenant isolation, and exactly what each actor sees and can do - merchant, finance operator, admin.
Work With Provider Documentation: Read integration docs from payment providers and turn them into requirements the team can build against.

Will Be a Plus

PSP & Acquiring Background: 3DS protocols, chargebacks, settlement reconciliation, provider cascades, routing rules.
Greenfield Experience: Building a product area from scratch, where the process doesn't exist yet and has to be designed alongside the feature.
Regulatory Awareness: PCI DSS, AML, sanctions screening - understanding why certain data can't be logged or exported.
Competitive Analysis: Benchmarking a product against market players and turning gaps into a roadmap.

Format: Full-time

Start date: As soon as possible

Location: Remote

new_jobs.title: Senior Operations Analyst for Undersea Warfare
new_jobs.description:
Description

Do you have experience investigating and solving complex issues, and conveying analysis to a variety of audiences?

Are you interested in applying your skills to critical problems supporting national security?

If so, we 're looking for someone like you to join our team at APL.

We are seeking an experienced operations analyst to provide technical contributions and leadership to support continued American all-domain and joint warfare superiority. We are a hardworking team of analysts and operators who apply the latest technology to important problems supporting the US Navy Sea Control Mission. Our group strives to cultivate an environment of innovation and collaboration while working on complex technical challenges that contribute to the security of the United States!

As a Senior Operations Analyst for Undersea Warfare...

Your primary responsibility will be to analyze and evaluate Concepts of Operations (CONOPs) of Surface Warfare (SUW), Undersea Warfare (USW) and Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) platforms and sensors.
You will provide technical contributions in the form of problem definition, requirements and metrics development, system assessment, analysis of mission success, and documentation.
You will work with analysis team and systems authorities to evaluate and assess measures of performance and measures of effectiveness for SUW, USW and ASW systems.
You will conduct evaluation of factors such as system performance, logistic requirements, costs, operational impacts, and potential CONOPs, the results of which will be detailed in reports and annotated briefs for delivery to Department of War (DoW) sponsors.
You will interact with DoW and or Navy staff to facilitate task execution and work prioritization. This includes briefing the sponsor or DoW command staff on the insights of the work and possible participation in field tests or sea trials for SUW, USW or ASW platforms and sensors.

Qualifications

You meet our minimum qualifications for the job if you...

Have a Bachelor 's Degree with ten or more years of relevant USW/ASW operational/technical experience.
Are technically and analytically oriented and possess curiosity about both current and future SUW/USW/ASW systems and work well in a team environment with a proven ability to lead small teams.
Have initiative, motivation and flexibility, and possess strong analytical, operational, problem-solving and organizational skills.
Are willing and able to travel (i.e., occasional 2-3 day trips or week long tests), are willing to work on dynamic projects, and can prioritize a number of concurrent taskings.
Hold an active Secret security clearance and can ultimately obtain a TS/SCI level clearance. If selected, you will be subject to a government security clearance investigation and must meet the requirements for access to classified information. Eligibility requirements include U.S. citizenship.

You 'll go above and beyond our minimum requirements if you...

Have a Master's degree in Engineering, Physics, Applied Mathematics, Operations Research or relevant technical field.
Have held Commander Command, Major Command and/or sequential Command responsibilities.
Have worked under a Combatant Command Staff and have understanding of Operational Planning and battle management command and control and joint planning processes, procedures and functions.
Have experience working on Navy or Joint staffs and have familiarity with acquisition processes.
Have demonstrated understanding of features and patterns in data that identify the characteristics and behaviors of systems or components.
Have a current Top Secret or higher level security clearance.
Possess a good understanding of potential adversary defensive and offensive capabilities.

About Us

Why Work at APL?

The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) brings world-class expertise to our nation’s most critical defense, security, space and science challenges. While we are dedicated to solving complex challenges and pioneering new technologies, what makes us truly outstanding is our culture. We offer a vibrant, welcoming atmosphere where you can bring your authentic self to work, continue to grow, and build strong connections with inspiring teammates.

At APL, we celebrate our differences of perspectives and encourage creativity and bold, new ideas. Our employees enjoy generous benefits, including a robust education assistance program, unparalleled retirement contributions, and a healthy work/life balance. APL’s campus is located in the Baltimore-Washington metro area. Learn more about our career opportunities at https://www.jhuapl.edu/careers.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, creed, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, occupation, marital or familial status, political opinion, personal appearance, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. APL is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to individuals of all abilities, including those with disabilities. If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in any part of the hiring process, please contact Accessibility@jhuapl.edu.

The referenced pay range is based on JHU APL’s good faith belief at the time of posting. Actual compensation may vary based on factors such as geographic location, work experience, market conditions, education/training and skill level with consideration for internal parity.
